lesson.title: Vector databases: the recall, memory and latency contract
lesson.short: Exact search · HNSW/IVF/PQ · GPU graphs · filtered top-k
lesson.timeMeaning: Suggested independent study minutes; not scheduled contact time
lesson.lead: Approximation is a choice about which candidates you can afford to miss. A vector database must also handle filters, versions, updates and access rules.
goals: Define exact top-k and ANN recall using the same metric and filter.
Compare graph traversal, inverted-file pruning and vector compression.
Design a recall-matched single-GPU experiment and explain multi-GPU limits.

sections.title: Start here: prerequisites and course status
sections.html:
Suppose a search returns five documents in 2 ms. Another returns five in 3 ms. Before choosing the faster search, we need to know which documents should have been returned. This lesson builds that answer first, then shows how an index trades search work for missed neighbors.

You only need vectors as lists of numbers and the purpose of an index. Numerical examples are original teaching examples. GPU implementation is optional. This supplemental companion is not an Edinburgh lecture or verified Canvas assignment; assigned readings, assessment rules, deadlines and submission arrangements remain unverified.

sections.title: Start with exact semantics
sections.html:
Start with q=(1,0) and two objects A=(1,0), B=(0,1). Squared Euclidean distance adds squared coordinate differences: d²(q,A)=0²+0²=0; d²(q,B)=1²+(−1)²=2. Smaller means closer. Inner product adds coordinate products: q·A=1, q·B=0; here larger means more similar.

Both objects and q have unit length. For unit vectors, d²=2−2(q·x), so maximizing inner product also minimizes distance and cosine distance. Without normalization the rankings can differ. Declare metric, preprocessing, numeric representation and tie-breaking before making a reference answer.

An exact top-k search chooses the k best eligible IDs under that definition. An approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANN) saves work by not examining everything or by approximating distances. If the exact top-5 is {A,B,C,D,E} and ANN returns {A,C,E,G,H}, their intersection is {A,C,E}; recall@5=3/5=0.6. Returning five objects does not mean finding all five correct neighbors.

Key takeaway

Separate embedding relevance, nearest-neighbor recall and downstream task accuracy. They measure different failure modes.

sections.title: Three complementary design choices
sections.html:
Why can ANN avoid a full scan? One strategy stores neighbor links. Starting at a graph node, compare nearby candidates, follow promising links and keep a shortlist. Exploring more nodes spends more distance calculations and memory traffic, usually improving recall. Construction and updates also cost work.

A second strategy groups vectors into clusters. Search only selected clusters rather than the entire collection: this is an inverted-file index (IVF). More probes inspect more candidates; a query near a cluster boundary can lose a close neighbor in an unvisited cluster.

A third strategy replaces full vectors with compact codes: quantization. It saves memory and estimates distance cheaply, but estimates can reverse two near-tied objects. Reranking a shortlist with original vectors corrects their distances, not neighbors omitted from that shortlist. These mechanisms can combine: IVF with quantized codes, or a graph with compressed vectors.

Compare against an exact scan, especially with small collections or large GPU batches. A vector database must also persist IDs, metadata, deletes and embedding versions, enforce access rules and coordinate concurrent operations. A faster search kernel alone does not establish a faster complete database.

Sources for this section: pgvector official repository documentation. Numerical traces marked original are teaching examples, not reported measurements.

sections.title: Worked example: recall and filtering
sections.html:
Now change eligibility. Keep the unfiltered exact top-5 {A,B,C,D,E}, but suppose a tenant filter permits only {B,D,F,G,H}. We must compute the best neighbors inside the permitted subset. The unfiltered reference is now the wrong answer to a different question.

Filtering after ANN can leave too few results. In an original model with independent 1% acceptance, 100 candidates leave 100×0.01=1 survivor on average. Retrieving 1,000 gives an expectation of ten, not a guarantee. Geometry and metadata can correlate, invalidating independence. Possible responses include iterative expansion, filter-aware search or exact search of the eligible subset.

Enforce access control before exposing protected results or payloads. Define how snapshots, deleted IDs and changed embeddings become visible; then test freshness separately from recall.

After filtering, three returned IDs all belong to exact filtered top-10. Is recall 1?

No. With at least ten eligible items, intersection size is three and denominator is ten: recall@10=0.3. Precision among those three is perfect, but seven required neighbors were missed. If fewer than k eligible objects exist, state a separate denominator convention.

sections.title: Read two recent approaches
sections.html:
The preceding mechanisms help separate two research contributions. CAGRA designs GPU graph construction and traversal. Its results depend on datasets, baselines, hardware, search settings and batch sizes. They are author-reported comparisons, not promised H100 performance in this exercise.

RaBitQ focuses on compact representation and bounded distance estimation. Its main coordinate code uses one bit per dimension, but surrounding scale information, IDs, links and optional reranking vectors still take space. An error bound on a distance estimate is not a promise that arbitrary candidate search returns the exact top-k.

Try this reasoning: if two candidates' true distances are 1.00 and 1.01, estimation error can swap their order. Even perfect reranking cannot recover a true neighbor never considered. Ask whether your bottleneck is traversal, representation capacity, bandwidth, arithmetic or construction before selecting a paper's mechanism. Read implementation guides at a pinned version; current software need not reproduce the original artifact.

Sources for this section: CAGRA (ICDE 2024); RaBitQ (SIGMOD 2024). Numerical traces marked original are teaching examples, not reported measurements.

sections.title: H100-sized mini-experiment: one GPU first
sections.html:
First choose the quality requirement. In an original paper checkpoint, low effort returns {A,C,E,G,H} in a hypothetical 2 ms; high effort returns {A,B,C,D,E} in 3 ms. Against exact {A,B,C,D,E}, recall is 0.6 versus 1.0. At required recall≥0.95 only high effort qualifies. The 2 ms point cannot be advertised as faster at equal quality.

Before a GPU run, budget one million 768-dimensional FP32 vectors: 1,000,000×768×4=3,072,000,000 bytes=3.072 GB decimal. Degree-64 links with four-byte IDs add 1,000,000×64×4=0.256 GB. The sum 3.328 GB omits workspace, copies, buffers, allocator and other metadata; it is not measured peak memory.

Optional one-H100 work can compare exact GPU scan, IVF-Flat or IVF-PQ, and CAGRA at matched metric, data and recall. Separate validation tuning from held-out queries. Measure build time, peak memory, batch size, latency distribution, throughput and host-device transfers. Check actual free memory and pinned software/platform requirements first. Two H100s require explicit placement and communication measurements; they do not automatically pool memory or double speed.

Sources for this section: NVIDIA cuVS: CAGRA guide; NVIDIA cuVS: Benchmarking methodologies; NVIDIA cuVS: Installation. Numerical traces marked original are teaching examples, not reported measurements.

The current cuVS installation guidance has Linux packages and a WSL2 route for Windows, rather than native Windows support. Pin a release and compatible GPU/CUDA stack before running. A two-device extension should distinguish replicas from partitioned indexes: replicas may raise throughput, whereas partitions need routing and result merging. Include update/delete freshness, construction cost and peak memory in either case.

sections.title: Exercises, failure cases and takeaways
sections.html:
Keep one record per configuration: dataset and query split, preprocessing, index version, build/search settings, recall, timing boundary, batch size and memory. This lets another reader see why a setting is useful rather than remember one QPS number.

A gives 20,000 queries/s at recall 0.80; B gives 12,000 at 0.96. Which wins at equal quality?

The measurements cannot answer that. Sweep settings and compare where both meet the same target, or show a Pareto frontier: points for which improving one metric requires worsening another. A is faster at its reported, lower-quality point.

Does a one-bit code make the entire database 32× smaller than FP32?

Only the raw coordinate-code ratio is 32:1. Add scales, centroids, links, IDs, metadata and any originals used for reranking. Measure the complete footprint and construction peak. Also check filtered queries, updates and near ties before transferring the conclusion to a new workload.

Key takeaway

An honest ANN result reports recall, workload, batch size, latency/throughput, build cost and memory together.

quiz.question: The exact top-10 and returned top-10 share eight IDs. What is recall@10?
options: It cannot be computed without distance values.
quiz.explanation: The intersection contains eight required IDs, and ten exact eligible neighbors were requested. Recall@10=8/10=0.8. The two extra returned IDs do not recover the two missing required neighbors.

questions.question: An ANN result returns three correct neighbors when ten eligible exact neighbors exist. What is recall@10?
questions.explanation: Three correct returned IDs give an intersection of three. With ten eligible exact neighbors, recall@10=3/10=0.3. The denominator remains ten even when only three results are returned; all three being correct describes precision among the returned items.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: Which comparison isolates ANN speed at similar quality?
options: A parameter sweep followed by comparison at matched recall.
Highest QPS from each method regardless of recall.
A comparison with different distance metrics.
The smallest index without checking returned IDs.
questions.explanation: Search effort can buy recall with extra work. First tune on validation data, then compare held-out latency/throughput at a shared recall target and matched metric, data and batch size. Faster at lower recall does not isolate a speed improvement at equal quality.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: What is the FP32 coordinate payload for 1,000,000 vectors with 768 dimensions, in decimal GB?
questions.explanation: FP32 uses four bytes per coordinate: 1,000,000×768×4=3,072,000,000 bytes=3.072 decimal GB. This is only coordinate payload. Degree-64 four-byte links add 0.256 GB before workspace, copies, metadata and other buffers; it is not measured peak memory.
questions.origin: Original supplemental exercise; not a verified assessed question

questions.question: When do cosine and squared Euclidean rankings agree through the identity 2−2·dot-product?
options: Only when approximate search is disabled.
Only for vectors with negative coordinates.
For all arbitrary vectors without preprocessing.
questions.explanation: For nonzero vectors normalized to unit length, squared Euclidean distance is 2−2(q·x). Thus larger dot product means smaller squared distance and the same cosine ranking. Without normalization, differing vector lengths can change these rankings.
